extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who practice before the USPTO (particularly those not registered for patent practice), OED staff, and USPTO disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO attorney discipline for unauthorized practice
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving USPTO disciplinary action for an attorney who assisted in preparing and filing provisional patent applications while not registered to practice patent matters; sets out jurisdiction, applicable rules, stipulated facts, legal conclusions, mitigating/aggravating factors, and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory and regulatory bases for OED and the USPTO Director to assert authority to investigate and resolve practitioner discipline; required citation when bringing or defending disciplinary matters before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners appearing before the Office must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.; these rules form the substantive standards of professional behavior evaluated in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'practice before the Office' (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1) governs the definition of practice before the Office in patent matters; Respondent did not fully understand or appreciate the breadth of this provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assisting in preparing and filing patent (including provisional) applications can fall within the definition of practice before the Office; lack of understanding of § 11.5(b)(1) does not excuse conduct. The regulation's scope should be reviewed by practitioners to determine when actions constitute practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of patent law (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assisting in preparing and filing patent applications while not registered to practice before the Office constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 — unauthorized practice of patent law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds that Respondent's providing input and assistance in preparing and filing seven provisional patent applications over a forty-six month period violated § 11.505. The Order demonstrates that such assistance, even when done at a client's direction or with the client's knowledge, can constitute unauthorized practice if the person is not authorized/registered for patent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors relevant to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors the Office considered in determining discipline included: lack of intent to violate USPTO rules; not done for financial gain (clients were not charged); immediate commitment to cease practice once informed of the rule; full cooperation with OED's investigation (including participating in an online interview); acknowledgment of lack of understanding; genuine contrition; acceptance of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating circumstances supported imposition of a public reprimand rather than more severe sanctions. Practitioners facing discipline should present cooperation, contrition, lack of intent, absence of personal financial gain, and prompt remedial steps when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of respondent's record in future proceedings (aggravating/rebuttal use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings concerning the Respondent — either as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements/representations by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary records can be used against a practitioner in subsequent matters; settlement and lesser sanction now may nonetheless be treated as aggravating in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedies the Office may impose/publish
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreed-upon sanction in this case: Respondent be publicly reprimanded; the OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room; the OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Public Reprimand text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common disciplinary remedies include public reprimand and publication of the order and notice in official outlets (FOIA Reading Room, Official Gazette). The Order includes a model notice and specifies publication venues and content. The parties also agreed each shall bear their own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights and finality of settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may include express waivers of review and appeal rights; practitioners entering settlements should be aware that such waivers render the disciplinary resolution final and preclude further administrative challenge under specified regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural service/certification of the Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service specifying methods of service (e.g., first-class certified mail, return receipt requested; e-mail) and identifies parties and addresses served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service of disciplinary orders and notices is required and memorialized in the record; documentation of service methods and recipients is part of the procedural requirements for enforcement and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's registration status as a determining fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was not registered to practice before the Office in patent matters (though licensed in state bars and practicing in trademark matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's registration status before the USPTO is central to determining whether particular activities (e.g., preparing/filing patent applications) constitute unauthorized practice; lawyers licensed in state courts but not registered with USPTO may still face discipline for patent-related activities that fall within 'practice before the Office.'
